description: Progressive QGIS/KADAS automation benchmarks for comparing Claude against raw and upskilled local models. Every tool name in 'expected_api_calls' and 'tools' was verified to exist in geoagent/tools/ on 2026-07-16.

conventions.eval_criteria: ADVISORY ONLY. These checks are a triage aid, not a verdict. A test is judged by a human looking at the screenshot and the raw output. See run_evals.py.
conventions.tools: The tool subset this test needs. The runner narrows the agent's surface to it, because the full 62-tool surface costs ~10.6k tokens and overflows a local 8k-16k context. See research/hardware_limitations.md.
conventions.backend: 'kadas' requires a live KADAS window (KADAS-native annotations, MilX, geoadmin). 'qgis' would run against plain QGIS, but no test currently claims it.
conventions.crs: KADAS is LV95/EPSG:2056 oriented. Lon/lat inputs are WGS84/EPSG:4326 unless stated.

benchmarks.prompt: List all the layers currently loaded in the project.

eval_criteria.human_check: Did it just answer, or did it wander off adding layers first? This is the smoke test: if a model fails E01 it cannot call a tool at all and the rest of the sweep is noise.

benchmarks.prompt: Add an OpenStreetMap basemap to the map.

eval_criteria.human_check: Is a basemap visible in the screenshot? A model that hand-rolls add_xyz_tile_layer with a tile URL instead of using add_osm_basemap is a partial pass, and is exactly the gap a skill should close.
eval_criteria.known_trap: Earlier XYZ URI brace-escaping bugs made layers load but render blank. Trust the screenshot over the tool's success message.

eval_criteria.human_check: Is Zurich actually centred and at a sensible scale? locate_and_zoom is one call; a model doing search_location then set_center then set_scale is working harder than needed.

benchmarks.prompt: Load the swisstopo national map (colour) background layer.

eval_criteria.human_check: Did it search the catalog first, or guess a layer id? Guessing a swisstopo bodid from memory is the classic local-model failure here and the strongest argument for a geoadmin skill.

benchmarks.prompt: Convert the WGS84 coordinates 8.5417, 47.3769 to Swiss LV95.

eval_criteria.human_check: Expected LV95 is roughly E 2683000, N 1247000. A model that computes this in its head instead of calling the tool must be marked FAIL even if the number looks right: it is guessing, and it will be wrong elsewhere.

benchmarks.prompt: Remove every layer from the project, then confirm it is empty.

eval_criteria.human_check: Tests multi-step planning and loop-until-done. Does it enumerate first, then remove each, then verify? Or remove one and claim success?

benchmarks.prompt: Place a marker on Bern labelled 'HQ'.

eval_criteria.human_check: Is the marker on Bern and labelled 'HQ'? Screenshot is authoritative: annotation tools report success even when the item renders off-screen. One call should do it — add_map_marker takes the label directly, so a model that adds a marker AND a separate add_text_annotation is doing redundant work.
eval_criteria.known_trap: VERIFIED signature: add_map_marker(lon*, lat*, label) — there is NO colour argument. The prompt deliberately does not ask for a colour. If you re-add 'red' to this prompt, every agent will either fail or lie about it; marker styling is a genuine tool-surface gap, not a model failure.

benchmarks.prompt: Draw a circle with a 5 km radius centred on Interlaken.

eval_criteria.human_check: Is the drawn circle actually 5 km across the map? add_map_circle(lon, lat, radius_m) names the unit in the argument, so this is easier than it looks; the failure to watch for is unit confusion (passing 5 instead of 5000) or lon/lat swapped, which puts the circle in the wrong hemisphere.
eval_criteria.known_trap: VERIFIED signature: add_map_circle(lon*, lat*, radius_m*) — takes WGS84 degrees for the centre and METRES for the radius. The argument name carries the unit, so a well-behaved model should get this right. If a local model still passes degrees as radius_m, that is a strong signal it is ignoring the schema.

benchmarks.prompt: What is the elevation at the summit of the Matterhorn?

eval_criteria.human_check: True summit is ~4478 m. Accept 4470-4490 (DTM sampling varies). A model that answers 4478 from memory without calling get_elevation_at is a FAIL: it did not query the terrain, it recalled a fact.

benchmarks.prompt: Find all hospitals in Bern and add them to the map.

eval_criteria.human_check: Did it build a sane Overpass query (amenity=hospital, bbox around Bern)? Overpass rejects malformed QL loudly, so failures here are usually visible in the tool result.

benchmarks.prompt: Add a hillshade layer for the area around Grindelwald.

eval_criteria.human_check: Tests dependency reasoning: hillshade needs a DTM loaded first. Does the model realise it must load terrain before shading it, or does it call create_hillshade_layer against nothing?

benchmarks.prompt: Is there a clear line of sight from the summit of the Niesen to the summit of the Stockhorn?

eval_criteria.human_check: Multi-step: resolve two summits to coordinates, then run LOS and interpret the profile. Niesen ~2362 m, Stockhorn ~2190 m, ~15 km apart. VERIFIED signature: check_line_of_sight(observer_lon*, observer_lat*, target_lon*, target_lat*, observer_height_m, target_height_m, terrain_samples) — it takes WGS84 degrees, NOT LV95. The interesting failure is a model 'helpfully' converting to LV95 first and passing metres into a degrees argument, or swapping observer/target lon/lat.

benchmarks.prompt: Place a friendly infantry unit MilX symbol at Thun.

eval_criteria.human_check: EXPECTED TO FAIL FOR EVERY AGENT, Claude included. Do not read a failure here as a model deficiency. The ONLY reachable path is list_kadas_actions -> trigger_kadas_action, which activates a MilX map tool that then waits for interactive mouse input — so an agent cannot complete the placement unattended. Read the raw output for what it *attempted*; that is the design input for a real MilX tool.
eval_criteria.known_trap: VERIFIED 2026-07-16: run_pyqgis_script AST-validates imports against _PYQGIS_ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL = {'qgis', 'math'} (geoagent/tools/qgis.py:32), so `import kadasgui` is REJECTED. The PyQGIS route to KadasMilxAnnotationItem is closed by design. Conclusion is already known without running this: GeoAgent needs a first-class MilX tool. This test exists to document that gap, not to discover it.

benchmarks.prompt: List the MilX layers in this project and tell me how many symbols each contains.

eval_criteria.human_check: Read-only counterpart to H02. Requires a project with MilX layers preloaded, otherwise the correct answer is 'none'. Tests whether the model reaches for the KADAS-native introspection tools rather than list_project_layers.
eval_criteria.setup: Load a .milx package before running, or expect an empty-but-correct answer.

benchmarks.prompt: Create a 10 km buffer around Lake Thun, clip the swisstopo DTM to it, and tell me the highest point inside.

eval_criteria.human_check: The hardest test: chain geocode -> buffer -> load DTM -> clip -> zonal max. Expect local models to fail entirely. Grade partial credit by how far down the chain it got, and record where it broke; that is the skill-authoring signal.
